docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Produce a multi-page, print-ready HTML infographic titled "A day in the life of a developer using 3C." It tells the working day of one engineer (call her Maya) who is shipping inside a team that has adopted 3C — Claude Code Coach at L2 (v1.5.0, May 2026), and it makes the workflow legible at a glance: one phase per page, one diagram per phase, one key message per phase.

The deliverable is a standalone .html file that mirrors the structure, design system, and print posture of site/infographic/sdlc-infographic.html — same A4 portrait pages, same typography, same colour tokens, same badge / title / diagram / key- message / footer rhythm — so the new infographic sits next to the existing one as a sibling deliverable, not a one-off.

docs.title: Audience
docs.text: A new engineer joining a team that already runs 3C at L2. Assumes general familiarity with Git, sprint-based agile workflows, TDD, and PR review, plus everyday use of Claude Code as her AI assistant — but zero prior knowledge of 3C itself, its slash commands, its rule files, its subagents, or its gate chain.

docs.title: Hard constraints — Maya never edits code or tests by hand
docs.text:
This is non-negotiable, and the writer must read this section before starting the diagrams.

Maya is an instructor, not a typist. Every code change, every test change, every fix, every refactor in this infographic happens through Claude Code (her AI assistant) or through one of the /3c-* slash commands — never by Maya opening a file in her IDE and editing it manually. This is true even for:

  • writing the assertions in a TDD test (she prompts /3c-test or Claude Code with the assertions she wants in natural language; the skill or the assistant types them)
  • fixing a failing test (she re-prompts Claude Code with the diagnosis, or dispatches the architect / code-reviewer subagent for a second opinion, and lets the assistant apply the fix)
  • tightening an issue body that came back too vague (she iterates with /3c-create-issue until it is right)
  • correcting a coaching-mode rule violation (she re-prompts Claude Code with the rationale she just read in the coaching segment)

Maya does type freely in three places, and only these three:

  1. Prompts — to Claude Code, to the slash commands, to subagents.
  2. Issue / PR comments in GitHub.
  3. Config-style decisions — picking the next issue, choosing a branch name, approving a destructive-operation prompt with y, running /3c-bypass --reason="..." for a real hot-fix.

If a phase seems to demand hand-editing, that is a signal the phase is under-specified — re-prompt or re-dispatch instead. The infographic should reinforce this discipline visibly: in every diagram, the arrow that changes code is labelled with the slash command or the assistant that did the typing.

docs.title: What to establish on the cover page
docs.text:
Before the seven phase pages, a cover page establishes:

  • The premise. 3C is AI engineering alignment: keeping every team member's AI assistant working from the same conventions, the same workflow, and the same quality bar. Without it, every session is locally optimal but the aggregate is locally optimal, globally incoherent (site/why-now.html).
  • The three pillars — Standards (CLAUDE.md under a hard 150-instruction cognitive budget, .claude/rules/, the architecture pattern library, the security policy templates), Workflow (the slash commands), Quality (the gate chain). site/diagrams/pillars.svg may be inlined or recreated as a small inset.
  • The L2 surface area Maya uses today — slash commands /3c-create-issue, /3c-implement, /3c-review, /3c-test, /3c-drift, /3c-standards history, /3c-explain <rule-id>, /3c-deploy, /3c-bug, /3c-onboard, /3c-onboard-guide, /3c-bypass; the crew orchestrators /3c-review-board, /3c-project-manager, /3c-programme-manager; the eight review agents architect, code-reviewer, security-reviewer, test-author, product-owner, ux-expert, qa-reviewer, journey-architect; gate chain Post-Edit Validation (< 300 ms) → Pre-Commit (< 10 s) → Coverage Gate + Security Scan Gate (< 60 s) → Drift Detector (on-demand).
  • Coaching mode — ON by default; teaching segment shape (——— 3c coaching ——— block) shown verbatim in a sidebar so the reader recognises it later; goes terse after TERSE_AFTER = 2 sightings of the same rule by the same developer.
  • The brand caveat (one line, drawn from site/branding.html) — if this team has run npx 3c init --brand="Acme" and chosen the slug acme, the reader will see /acme-review in their terminal instead of /3c-review; the slash prefix is brand-controlled, the upstream code is not. The infographic uses the unbranded /3c-* names throughout for clarity.
  • The honesty discipline — 3C deliberately under-claims; reversal is git revert of one PR; no source code leaves the workstation.

docs.text:

The writer should commit a .mmd file per diagram into site/infographic/diagrams/ following the existing naming pattern (f-intake.mmd, g-enrichment.mmd, h-batch.mmd, i-sprint-assembly.mmd, j-implement.mmd, k-sprint-throughput.mmd, l-uat.mmd, m-dashboard.mmd), pre-render each to SVG with the same toolchain (puppeteer.config.json is already in the folder), and inline the SVGs into the HTML at the <!--SVG_F--> style placeholders.

Every mermaid source must begin with the same %%{init: ...}%% theme block the existing five diagrams use, so the typography and palette match. Pick the right diagram type per phase:

docs.title: Diagram F — Phase 1 — Intake → issue creation (flowchart TD)
docs.text: Nodes: PM Brief, Slack Thread, CSV (customer feedback) → /3c-create-issue prompt → iteration loop → GitHub Issue (structured: title, user-story, scope, out-of-scope, ACs, deps, source- link). Label the iteration arrow Maya re-prompts /3c-create-issue explicitly. Annotate the GitHub Issue node with the 6 required fields as a sub-list. Footer reference: L2 Multi-PM MCP adapter · GitHub default at L1.

docs.title: Diagram G — Phase 2 — Technical enrichment (sequenceDiagram)
docs.text: Actors: Maya, architect (subagent), /3c-explain (skill), GitHub Issue. Steps: Maya dispatches architect with the issue context; architect returns affected components / approach / risks / open questions / complexity / testing strategy; Maya reads, identifies one proposed pattern that doesn't fit the codebase, runs /3c-explain <rule-id> against a rule she's not sure about, pushes back to architect with the rationale, gets a revised analysis, appends it to the GitHub Issue. Critical: no node labelled "Maya edits the analysis" — every change to the analysis is made by architect after Maya's prompt or by /3c-implement later.

docs.title: Diagram H — Phase 3 — Batch backlog refinement (flowchart LR)
docs.text: Funnel: 18 raw items → batch prompt template → /3c-create-issue ×18 → near-duplicate detection (a diamond decision node; merged duplicates loop back into the count) → human-clarification flag (a small branch off for items that are internally contradictory or missing context — these do not proceed) → /3c-drift check that no issue references a non-existent rule → cleaned set (e.g. 12 ready, 4 merged, 2 flagged for human clarification). The diagram makes the funnel shape visible: 18 in, 12 out, with the lost mass labelled.

docs.title: Diagram I — Phase 4 — Sprint assembly (flowchart TB)
docs.text: A 5-check grid above a single output node. Top row, left to right: overlap scan, AC contradiction scan, missing-deps scan, coverage-gap scan, doc-uniformity scan — each invoked by /3c-review adapted for sprint scope, with /3c-standards history as a side-node feeding all five. Bottom node: Tightened sprint (deduplicated, internally consistent) with one issue explicitly punted (a side-arrow labelled needs ADR-level discussion).

docs.title: Diagram J — Phase 5 — One issue, end-to-end (stateDiagram-v2)
docs.text: The most detailed diagram — give it the .xl diagram-wrap class. States, in order: Issue selected → /3c-implement plan → branch created → /3c-test scaffolds failing tests → Claude Code implements → Post-Edit Validator (<300ms) → loop back to Claude Code on failure → git stage + commit → Pre-Commit Hook (<10s) (lint / types / unit / secret) → loop back on failure with coaching segment shown → Coverage Gate + Security Scan Gate (<60s) → /3c-implement PR description → /3c-review-board → eight-agent panel (architect, code-reviewer, security-reviewer, test-author, product-owner, ux-expert, qa-reviewer, journey-architect) → reconciled verdict (blocking / advisory / clean) → Maya prompts Claude Code to apply the applicable findings → merge to main. Show the verdict as advisory — Maya still decides. Every edge that changes code is labelled with who typed it (Claude Code applies, /3c-implement applies, /3c-test scaffolds) — never Maya.

docs.title: Diagram K — Phase 6 — Working the rest of the sprint (flowchart TD)
docs.text:
A compounding loop: Issue 2 → Issue 3 → Issue 4, each running through a compact box labelled /3c-implement (full loop, see Diagram J). Off to the side, three loops that get tighter each iteration: - Coaching loop: verbose teaching segment on issue 2 → terse on issue 4 (annotate TERSE_AFTER = 2). - Pattern-reuse loop: prompt to /3c-implement references the merged PR ("follow the shape of #1284") — no re-pasting of standards into context (annotate 150-instruction budget held). - Subagent loop: architect dispatched once for a hard design call; security-reviewer dispatched before PR for an auth-touching change.

A side-branch shows the hot-fix path: prod incident → /3c-bypass --reason="prod hotfix #INC-417" → JSONL event recorded → ship → follow-up issue auto-created.

A second side-branch shows the tricky-failure path (this is the one to design carefully so it stays consistent with the hard constraint above): Pre-Commit fails on tricky test → Maya reads coaching rationale → Maya prompts Claude Code: "the rule is right, the test asserts the wrong contract, regenerate it" → Claude Code revises the test → gate passes. No node labelled "Maya edits the test in IDE" — instead, the diagram makes visible that the rule's authority routes the fix through the assistant, not around it.

docs.title: Diagram L — Phase 7 — Manual end-user testing (sequenceDiagram)
docs.text: Actors: Maya, /3c-test --mode=integration, /3c-deploy, Staging environment, /3c-bug, GitHub Issue. Sequence: Maya invokes /3c-test --mode=integration for a UI/integration change → skill scaffolds a UAT checklist + edge cases (test-author subagent assists) → Maya invokes /3c-deploy --env=staging → deploy runs pre-flight checks → health check passes → Maya runs the checklist manually in staging → finds a regression → Maya invokes /3c-bug → skill captures OS, runtime, project state, recent commits, scrubbed env vars → structured report appended to original GitHub Issue → Maya comments and reopens or marks done. Annotate the production-deploy arrow with requires --yes.

docs.title: Diagram M — End-of-day reflection (pie or flowchart)
docs.text:
A small mock-up of the Personal Local Insights Dashboard at .3c/dashboard.html. Three panels: - Rules that fired most for me today (top 5 list) - First-try gate pass-rate (one big number, e.g. "78%") - Post-edit validation deltas trend (sparkline placeholder)

Annotate plainly: local-only · gitignored · never egressed at L2 · your manager cannot see this.

docs.title: Phase narratives — body copy under each diagram
docs.text:
The diagram carries the structure; the body copy (placed inside the .diagram-subtitle slot and, for richer phases, an additional small prose block above the .key-message) carries Maya's voice. Each phase narrative should:

  • Open with one sentence on what Maya is doing and why.
  • Show one concrete artifact verbatim in a .snippet block:
  • Phase 1 — the literal /3c-create-issue prompt she sends, then the resulting issue body (truncated to ~10 lines).
  • Phase 2 — the architect subagent's output snippet (3–4 bullet points), then a one-line /3c-explain <rule-id> invocation and its reply.
  • Phase 3 — the batch-prompt template (5 lines) and the human- clarification flag email/comment (2 lines).
  • Phase 4 — the /3c-review adapted prompt and its summary of findings (5 lines).

  • Phase 5 — the coaching teaching segment exactly as shipped:

    ——— 3c coaching ———
• import-order
Why:  imports should be ordered stdlib, third-party, local —
      fewer merge conflicts in long-lived branches.
Do:   import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
Docs: https://github.com/kgn-git/praise/blob/main/strategy/adr/AD-04-local-storage.md
———————————————

    plus a JSONL gate event verbatim (one line). - Phase 6 — a terse coaching segment (bullet + Why: only) and the JSONL bypass event with the reason field populated. - Phase 7 — a /3c-bug structured report header (5 lines, scrubbed). - Close with the three call-outs (as compact bullets, not boxes — the .key-message box already does the visual emphasis): - What 3C does for you here. - What Maya still owns here. (always a thinking / judgement action, never a typing action) - What 3C deliberately does NOT do here.

Cap each phase body copy at ~180 words so the page stays scannable and the diagram dominates.

docs.title: Closing page (page 9) — common mistakes + checklist
docs.text:
Two stacked sections inside the existing .closing layout:

Common mistakes — six cards (re-use the .takeaway-grid / .takeaway styles, but number them with a red .takeaway-num accent instead of indigo, and rename the class for the rendered file). Each card is one sentence on the mistake plus one sentence on the correction. Required mistakes:

  1. Rubber-stamping AI-generated issues; correction: read every issue body before publishing — /3c-create-issue produces what you prompt, not what you mean.
  2. Pasting the entire standards doc into prompts; correction: trust the .claude/rules/ library and the 150-instruction budget — re- pasting blows the budget and degrades the model.
  3. Bypassing without a real --reason; correction: the JSONL event is permanent and reviewable — "forgot why" in the reason field is how teams lose trust in the bypass mechanism.
  4. Treating coaching segments as noise; correction: the second sighting goes terse on its own — read it the first time and the framework gets quieter on its own.
  5. Running /3c-implement on issues that haven't been enriched; correction: enrich first (Phase 2), then implement — architect is cheaper before code than after.
  6. Trying to edit code or tests by hand to "save time"; correction: the assistant types, you instruct — every hand-edit is a missed opportunity for the rule library to evolve.

Pinnable checklist (single card spanning both columns, ≤ 20 lines). Required content, in this order:

  • Slash commands by phase: /3c-create-issue · /3c-explain · /3c-drift · /3c-review · /3c-standards history · /3c-implement · /3c-test [--mode=integration] · /3c-deploy --env=<…> · /3c-bug · /3c-bypass --reason="...".
  • Subagents and when to dispatch each: architect (design call), security-reviewer (auth/crypto/input-handling), code-reviewer (pre-PR findings), test-author (test scaffolding inside /3c-test), product-owner (scope/priority), ux-expert (screen-level UX), qa-reviewer (AC traceability), journey-architect (journey reachability) — or convene all eight at once with /3c-review-board, which reconciles their findings into one verdict.
  • Gate chain in firing order: Post-Edit Validation (< 300 ms) → Pre-Commit (< 10 s) → Coverage + Security Scan (< 60 s) → Drift (on-demand).
  • Bypass syntax: /3c-bypass --reason="<one-line>" — logged, never silent.
  • File paths to remember: CLAUDE.md (root, ≤ 150 instructions), .claude/rules/<rule>.rationale.yaml, .3c/coaching.yaml, .3c/coaching/<user>.yaml, .3c/events/*.jsonl, .3c/dashboard.html.
  • The one rule that summarises the rest: the assistant types, you instruct.

docs.title: PRAISE / 3C — Strategy Review & Proposed Backlog (2026-05-25)
docs.text:
Durable copy of the strategy review conducted on 2026-05-25 (via /project-manager). Covers roadmap status, the 3c: namespace + agents/skills diagnosis (root cause confirmed in code), Microsoft-repo lessons (Agent Governance Toolkit + AI Engineering Coach), the GUI-surface direction, and the enriched specs of the backlog issues opened on kgn-git/praise.

Namespace decision (settled): copy install is the only supported path (team edits skills post-retro), using a hyphen prefix (/3c-foo, or /<brand>-foo after a rebrand prompt). Update (later 2026-05-25): the colon namespace is dropped and the plugin/colon distribution path is retired — hyphen everywhere. Implemented via #240 (incl. AD-16 amendment to hyphen-only); the subagent path-guard is therefore registered solely via 3c hook install (#242). See §2.5.

docs.text: Five threads were raised: (1) a roadmap status request; (2) confusion that 3C installs as /create-issue not 3c:create-issue, and that the installed agents have no obvious way to be called; (3) an idea for an Electron setup app with five guided steps; (4) an instruction to review how those points fit the product strategy and prioritise them; and (5) a request to mine two new Microsoft releases for lessons.

docs.title: 2. The 3c: namespace + agents/skills — root cause (confirmed in code)
2a. Why you see /create-issue, not 3c:create-issue
docs.text:
3C has two install paths that behave differently:

Path How Namespace Copy/init (what you used) 3c skills install copies folders into .claude/skills/ None → /create-issue Plugin marketplace /plugin install using .claude-plugin/plugin.json (name: "3c") Colon → 3c:create-issue

Confirmed platform constraint: the colon namespace (name:command) is exclusively a plugin feature, driven by the name field in .claude-plugin/plugin.json. Copy-installed project skills cannot be colon-namespaced — Claude Code invokes them as bare /foo, with no override.

docs.title: 2b. The coherence bug (confirmed)
docs.text: On the copy path, brand tokens are substituted at install time (src/agents/install.ts:57, src/skills/install.ts:94). With no branding.json, the default slug = 3c. So agents install as 3c-architect and their docstrings reference /3c:review, but the skill installs unnamespaced as /review (skill name: has no prefix). The two halves point at a namespace that doesn't exist in copy mode. The skill bodies themselves are also full of /3c:<x> references (3C/templates/skills/review/SKILL.md:10,16, implement→/3c:test//3c:review, etc.).

docs.title: 2c. Why you can't "call" the agents
docs.text: You cannot invoke a subagent with a slash command. Skills = user-triggered slash commands. Agents = specialist workers a skill (or Claude) delegates to via the Task tool, in a fresh context; auto-selected by description. The four shipped agents (read-only critics + one writer) are each paired to a skill: architect/code-reviewer→/review, security-reviewer→/security, test-author→/test.

docs.title: 2d. The deeper confusion — 3C has TWO surfaces
docs.text:
• "Factory" (this dev repo's .claude/skills/): project-manager, product-owner, solution-architect, security-architect, plugin-architect, developer, backlog-builder. Builds PRAISE; never shipped.
  • "Product" (3C templates/): skills create-issue/implement/review/test/onboard/onboard-guide + agents architect/code-reviewer/security-reviewer/test-author. What adopters get. The requested roster (programme-manager/ui-expert/data-engineer/security-expert) exists in neither — addressed in Tier 2.

docs.title: 2.5 Decision: copy-install default + hyphen namespace — impact analysis
docs.text:
Decision: keep copy install as the default happy path so the team can evolve SKILL.md files from retrospectives (git-as-SoT; feeds Retrospective Skill #13). Use a hyphen pseudo-namespace (/3c-review; /<brand>-review after a rebrand prompt that sets 3c, default 3c). Plugin/colon install stays an optional alternative. Implementation note: add a single install-time separator token so the same templates render hyphen (copy) or colon (plugin) without forking content.

Surface Affected by hyphen? Impact & required action Skills Yes — directly Prefix dir + name: at install (/3c-review); flip every in-body /3c:<x> → - (headings, "invoked as", cross-skill calls implement→/3c-test//3c-review, onboard-guide→/3c-onboard). Upside: /3c-* groups in autocomplete, avoids collision with team's own /review. Biggest downstream risk: team edits clobbered by skills install --replace → needs merge/provenance story (VP-01-F09 + #13); flagged as follow-on. Agents Barely name: already hyphen (3c-architect) — no change. Skill→agent dispatch by name already hyphen+substituted — works. Auto-selection by description — unaffected. Only change: agent docstrings' paired-skill refs /3c:review → -. Cross-link: the read-only critics' sandbox depends on the path-guard hook (see Hooks) — that is the real agent risk, not naming. Hooks No (event matchers, no namespace) Command path is ${slug} hook run (brand-on-PATH, not ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}) — already copy-friendly (src/hooks/install.ts:43). ⚠️ Security regression from the decision: 3c hook install registers only the Bash pre-commit orchestrator; the subagent path-guard (matcher Read\|Edit\|Write, blocks .env/.ssh/.aws) is registered only by the plugin manifest (3C/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:16). On copy-default (no plugin) it is silently absent. → new T0-5. Rules No (not slash-invoked) Land in .claude/rules/<pack>/ with substitution (src/rules/install-pack.ts:65). Real impacts: (a) shared 150-instruction budget — team's retro rules + 3C packs compete; already warns at 120/150; (b) upgrade-clobber on --replace; (c) skill→rule path refs (review/checklist.md cites .claude/rules/patterns/*/) must track any dir reorg.

AD-16 reconciliation: AD-16 currently defines 3c as the colon slash-namespace via plugin name. Amend it to define a brand command-prefix with two encodings — hyphen (copy, default) / colon (plugin, optional) — both driven by the rebrand prompt setting 3c. Folded into T0-2.

Decision record (cross-checked against official Claude Code docs, 2026-05-25): copy-install + hyphen was chosen deliberately over the colon-namespace alternatives. The docs confirm: (a) colon namespacing is a plugin-only construct (standalone skills are bare /foo); (b) plugin install copies the plugin to ~/.claude/plugins/cache and runs from there, so repo edits need a commit → /plugin marketplace update → /reload-plugins cycle; (c) --plugin-dir gives live in-place editing and the colon namespace, but only as a per-session launch flag. None of the colon paths preserve the frictionless, live, git pull-only retro-editing the team requires of the workflow skills — hence copy + hyphen. The colon-namespace plugin model remains documented as a future option if priorities change. This also reconfirms T0-5: the path-guard hook references ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, which is undefined off the plugin path, so it must be registered into .claude/settings.json directly.

docs.title: 3. Lessons from the Microsoft releases
docs.text:
Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT) — governs what deployed agents may do at runtime (policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, sandboxing, Merkle audit). Complementary niche, not a competitor. Lessons: 1. agt doctor/verify/red-team CLI — an install-validation "doctor" is the cheapest, highest-value lesson; would have answered the namespace/agent questions instantly → Tier 0 3c doctor. 2. They built the audit-chain machinery we cut from L1 (Merkle logs, Decision BOMs) — validates parking VP-05, revisit at L3/L4 with AGT as market evidence. 3. OWASP Agentic Top 10 — the emerging standard AGT maps to; our reviewer tracks classic OWASP → small Tier 2 extension. 4. Policy-as-code (allow/deny/require_approval YAML) maps to VP-05-F06 (#43, L4); don't over-rotate — markdown-rules simplicity is a deliberate differentiator. 5. Microsoft ships a first-party Claude Code governance plugin — validates the plugin form-factor and raises the stakes on our packaging (note: our happy path is now copy, so packaging must keep parity).

AI Engineering Coach (AIEC) — a local-first VS Code extension that reads AI session logs → observability + coaching. Almost a built realisation of VP-04 + VP-06:

AIEC feature PRAISE equivalent Lesson Local-first, no data leaves machine Local-First Principle Validates our core constraint; a GUI can be local-first. Dashboard / scores / trends VP-04-F01/F03 (#31/#33) L3 dashboard has product validation. 45 editable markdown rules + playground Our rules + review checklist A rule editor/playground GUI is validated → feeds #28. Skill Finder (usage → reusable skills) VP-02-F10 #28 + VP-06-F05 #25 Usage-pattern mining is real → augment #28. Context Health (instruction-file audit) VP-01-F01 CLAUDE.md Generator We generate; they audit → add audit mode = part of 3c doctor. Agentic SDLC visualisation Steps 3/4/5 of the setup-app idea The "illustrate the workflows" ask is validated. .vsix extension (not Electron) — Form-factor lesson (§4). Gamification (XP, Bronze→Diamond) nothing today New adoption-lever hypothesis → Tier 2 note.

docs.title: 4. GUI surface direction (selected: local web app via daemon)
docs.text:
The five proposed steps are two products: (a) a setup & onboarding console (steps 1–5 — run occasionally) and (b) the observability dashboard (VP-04 — ongoing, for managers, already in L3). They should share one surface, not fork into two apps. A local web app is editor-agnostic and local-first — better than AIEC's VS Code-only extension, which would conflict with VP-01-F07 cross-platform.

Reconciliation with existing ADRs (resolve in an ADR before building): - AD-06 already decides the L3 dashboard = Next.js app + Grafana, backed by TimescaleDB (AD-05), fed by batched sync (AD-13), workstation canonical (AD-15). - The daemon is deferred to L2 in AD-03-amendment and not yet implemented; the backend doesn't exist (sync is a stub at src/telemetry/sync.ts). But local telemetry already exists: JSONL at .<brand>/telemetry/hooks/<date>.jsonl (src/telemetry/record.ts, writer.ts) with aggregation at src/dashboard/metrics.ts.

Proposed two-tier model (refines, doesn't contradict, AD-06): - Local tier (new): a 3c local web app reading local JSONL/SQLite — offline, no backend. Hosts both the setup/onboarding console and a local-first dashboard (AIEC-style). - Aggregation tier (AD-06, unchanged): Next.js + TimescaleDB cross-team manager dashboard, fed by AD-13 sync from the local tier.

Needs AD-17: Local GUI surface tier + a new feature VP-06-F0x: Setup & Onboarding Console (roadmap gap). Both are Tier 1.
